🔐 NoName057(16) Claims DDoS Attack Against French Mobile Operator La Poste Mobile, but Disruption Re

sample_tweets.text: Refrigeration management systems across 700+ French 🇫🇷 supermarkets were compromised in October 2026, with attackers manipulating temperature and defrost controls to cause food losses at scale.  Key findings:  - The confirmed affected systems were Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland and Dixell XWEB. This is not a new threat: pro-Russian hacktivist groups Z-Pentest Alliance and NoName057(16) claimed over 20 refrigeration attacks since January 2026, mostly targeting fruit storage, wineries, and food processors across Spain 🇪🇸, Italy 🇮🇹, and other European countries. On April 26 alone, Z-Pentest claimed 10 separate hits. The attack method in each case was the same: changing temperature and defrost settings via exposed HMIs, using legitimate supervisory functions.  - Forescout's global exposure scan found 12,976 service observations across 6,017 distinct public IPs in 99 countries. The two attack paths are weak or absent authentication (only 287 of 513 pCOWeb services returned HTTP 401 responses) and known unpatched vulnerabilities. Danfoss AK-SM 800 is end-of-life since May 2021 with no patch path. For AK-SM 800A, 80% of exposed StoreView services run firmware older than 4.3.1, leaving them exposed to CVE-2025-41451 and CVE-2025-41452. Copeland XWEB Pro has 23 known vulnerabilities below firmware 1.13. CAREL products carry 11 known vulnerabilities across boss, boss mini, and pCOWeb.  - Initial access methods and responsible actors in the French 🇫🇷 incidents remain unconfirmed. Manufacturer documentation for both Danfoss AK-SM and Copeland XWEB explicitly supported direct internet exposure, port forwarding, and HTTP access for remote maintenance, meaning many installations are intentionally reachable. This creates a fractured ownership model: contractors manage the refrigeration platform, facilities teams own hardware, IT manages the network path, and no single party sees the full picture.  - Beyond setpoints, devices like CAREL pCOWeb and XWEB Pro expose Modbus-readable and writable variables, widening the impact potential. Rapid successive configuration changes observed in France 🇫🇷 suggest automation, meaning attackers scripted supervisory API calls rather than making manual adjustments, and those changes can blend into routine contractor activity with no obvious alert.  For responders and operators: the audit gap here is the correlation problem. A supervisory session log may not record which setpoint changed; a controller alarm may not identify the account behind it. Hunting for this activity means correlating remote-access session timestamps against defrost schedule changes, temperature setpoint modifications, alarm suppressions, and user account changes in the controller audit log. Review NAT and port-forwarding rules for port 80 and 443 terminating at refrigeration management interfaces. Prioritize replacing Danfoss AK-SM 800 (no patch exists) and patching AK-SM 800A to firmware 4.3.1 or later. The Forescout report details the full vulnerability table by product family.  #DFIR_Radar

Des difficultés d'accès ont été constatées sur plusieurs services de l'opérateur, notamment son site Internet, son espace client et la plateforme d'activation des cartes SIM.  Le groupe de hackers prorusse NoName057(16) revendique des attaques par déni de service, également appelées DDoS.  Cette technique consiste à saturer un service de requêtes pour le rendre inaccessible.  Le groupe affirme aussi posséder les données de 25 000 clients. 🇫🇷 🚨 FRANCE: NONAME057(16) CLAIMS DDOS ON LA POSTE MOBILE  The pro-Russian hacktivist group NoName057(16) claims it has knocked French mobile operator La Poste Mobile offline with a DDoS attack.  The group says it targeted La Poste Mobile's websites and its SIM card activation service. The claim was posted on October 21, 2026 under the group's #OpFrance campaign.  The claim has not been independently verified, and La Poste Mobile has not publicly confirmed any disruption.  The post follows a wave of DDoS claims against French government, energy, defense and maritime sites since mid-October. NoName057(16) also claimed the DDoS attack that disrupted La Poste group services in December 2025.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: DDoS claims are often brief and hard to verify, and hacktivist groups regularly overstate their impact. A DDoS attack floods services with traffic; it does NOT mean systems were breached or customer data was taken. What's reported: • CVE-2026-114625: SQL injection, CVSS 3.1 score 9.9 (critical) • Any authenticated user, down to the lowest Enterprise Read Only tenant role, can gain operator privileges as a local "superuser operator" • Exposed by default; no configuration prevents it • Arista detected the flaw and says it is known to be actively exploited • Hosted and Dedicated VCO already patched; on-prem fixed in 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10 and 6.4.2.12 • Attack IPs observed: 74.82.197.86 and 38.54.50.151  ⚠️ Analyst Note: This is Arista's fourth exploited VCO/EOS zero-day this year. A single stolen read-only tenant login is enough, so on-prem operators should patch now, restrict the VCO web UI to admin networks, and hunt logs for the listed IPs. Preserve logs before remediation if compromise is suspected.  Source: arista.com/en/support/adviso… #DDW #DarkWeb #Arista #VeloCloud #ZeroDay #CVE #SDWAN #PatchNow #CyberSecurity

⚠️ NODE.JS SECURITY RELEASES: BROTLI DECODER FLAW ENABLES REMOTE CODE EXECUTION (CVE-2026-111497)  The Node.js project shipped security releases on Oct 21, 2026 for all supported lines: 26.x, 24.x and 22.x.  What's reported: • CVE-2026-111497 (high): an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder permits remote code execution, affecting 26.x, 24.x and 22.x • CVE-2026-105483 and CVE-2026-106069 (high): TLS certificate hostname validation bypasses • CVE-2026-105482 (high): dns.resolve truncates names containing a NUL character • Several medium and low issues, including predictable crypto.randomUUID() values in startup snapshots and SEAs • Dependency updates for c-ares, OpenSSL, SQLite, Undici and the eMudhra intermediate CA distrust • Fixed in v26.12.1, v24.22.1 and v22.23.4  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Any service that decompresses untrusted Brotli input, such as HTTP responses or uploads, is the exposure to prioritize. Node.js has not reported exploitation in the wild. Upgrade runtimes and rebuild container images and bundled executables, since patching the host alone won't fix embedded runtimes.  Source: nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerabi… #DDW #DarkWeb #NodeJS #CVE #RCE #PatchNow #SupplyChain #CyberSecurity

🇪🇸 🚨 SPAIN: LAPSUS$-BRANDED ACTOR CLAIMS MADRID FOOTBALL FEDERATION DATA BREACH  A threat actor using the LAPSUS$ name is advertising a database they claim was stolen from the Real Federación de Fútbol de Madrid (RFFM), the governing body for football in the Madrid region.  The actor claims the data includes: * 100,000+ records from an internal database and document repository * 30,000+ scans of identity documents (DNI/NIE and passports) * Medical certificates * Home addresses, phone numbers and internal records  ⚠️ Analyst Note: ID document scans combined with medical certificates are high-value material for identity fraud. The LAPSUS$ name has been reused by unrelated actors before, so attribution is unconfirmed. 🇦🇷 🚨 ARGENTINA: THREAT ACTORS CLAIM 3M-RECORD CITIZEN DATABASE FROM SANTA FE PROVINCIAL GOVERNMENT  A threat actor group claims to have breached the provincial government of Santa Fe, Argentina, and is offering what it describes as the province's citizen database.  The actors claim: * About 3 million citizen records * A full database of about 2.5 GB * The data was listed on an underground forum  The claim has not been independently verified, and the Government of Santa Fe has not confirmed any incident.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: The post gives no sample fields, date range or proof of how the data was obtained. Argentine provincial governments have been named in a wave of underground claims in recent weeks, including Tucumán and Chaco, and some of these datasets turn out to be recycled or compiled from older leaks. We assess this as an unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a compromise of Santa Fe government systems. If authentic, citizen records at this scale could fuel identity fraud and phishing that impersonates provincial agencies.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Argentina #SantaFe #Government #DataLeak #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

LiteLLM suspects AI-gateway logs enabled its release compromise  LiteLLM says it observed Claude Code responses containing GitHub CLI OAuth tokens that could enter gateway logs.  It suspects attackers accessed its internet-facing internal LiteLLM deployment, stole tokens from those logs and hijacked the release workflow.  * An organization-owner token reportedly disabled branch protections. * A lookalike repository supplied the poisoned artifacts. * How attackers entered the gateway remains unconfirmed.  The October 21 release compromise is confirmed. This proposed initial-access chain is still under investigation, not proof of a Claude Code vulnerability.  docs.litellm.ai/blog/securit… #SupplyChainSecurity #AISecurity

The entry names the firm but marks the details as "to be announced", so no data volume, file list or samples have been published yet. A second, unrelated listing does not prove a breach, and it could reflect reused or third-party data. Treat this as an unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Ransomware #DataExtortion #KirklandEllis #LawFirm #LegalSector #DataLeak #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

ARTEX-linked attacks extend beyond the ConnectWise incident, Wiz reports  Wiz has documented related activity across multiple IT and software vendors during October, overlapping with Microsoft's Storm-0940 findings.  * Attackers probed account recovery, SSO and cross-tenant access. * Password spraying targeted Okta and Entra environments; Cognito flows were also tested. * Some sessions lasted 24–30 hours, switching addresses or endpoints when blocked.  Most attempts failed. This is evidence of sustained targeting, not a newly confirmed mass breach.  The practical lesson: correlate application and identity logs across repeated failures, rather than treating each probe in isolation.  wiz.io/blog/artex-in-the-wil… #AISecurity #ThreatIntelligence

🇬🇹 🚨 GUATEMALA: TERROAHGROUP CLAIMS BREACH OF ARMS-CONTROL AGENCY DIGECAM AND USAC UNIVERSITY  The threat actor TerroahGroup claims to have breached and exfiltrated databases from two Guatemalan institutions: DIGECAM (Dirección General de Control de Armas y Municiones), the state body that registers firearms and ammunition, and the Universidad de San Carlos de Guatemala (USAC), the country's main public university.  The actor claims: * Access to databases containing login credentials and user data * Ongoing monitoring of the affected portals * The targets were chosen over alleged security weaknesses  ⚠️ Analyst Note: If real, DIGECAM data could touch firearm and ammunition registration records, a serious security and regulatory risk. USAC data could expose students, faculty and staff. TerroahGroup has made a run of claims against Latin American government targets. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Guatemala #DIGECAM #USAC #DataBreach #ThreatIntelligence

🇵🇪 🚨 PERU: THREAT ACTOR LEAKS ALLEGED ESSALUD PATIENT DATABASE  A threat actor on a dark web forum has published a database they claim was stolen from EsSalud, Peru's public social health insurance agency, which covers millions of insured workers and their families.  The actor claims the data includes: * Full names, DNI (national ID) numbers, gender and addresses * Contact details * Medical record details and consultation notes * Patient complaints, internal system codes and user identifiers  ⚠️ Analyst Note: National ID numbers combined with medical history are high-value material for identity theft and health-themed phishing. The internal codes described could point to access to backend or administrative systems, but that is not confirmed. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation that EsSalud was breached.  #DDW #DarkWeb #EsSalud #Peru #DataBreach #Healthcare #ThreatIntelligence

🇯🇵 🚨 JAPAN: THREAT ACTOR CLAIMS 55 MILLION SOFTBANK CUSTOMER RECORDS FOR SALE  A threat actor on a dark web forum is offering a database they say holds 55 million records belonging to customers of SoftBank Corp., one of Japan's largest mobile carriers. The asking price is $500.  The actor claims the data includes: * Names, email addresses, phone numbers, street addresses and dates of birth * MSISDN, IMSI and ICCID (phone number and SIM identifiers), plan codes and device details * Billing data such as payment methods and monthly bill amounts  ⚠️ Analyst Note: SIM identifiers paired with identity and billing data are ideal material for SIM-swap fraud and convincing carrier-themed phishing. A low price for a dataset this size can point to recycled or inflated data, and a similar SoftBank listing showing only column names circulated earlier this month. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation that SoftBank was breached.  #DDW #DarkWeb #SoftBank #Japan #DataBreach #SIMSwap #ThreatIntelligence

PwC was also among the organizations named in Clop's 2023 MOVEit campaign. Everest has shifted toward data theft, insider recruitment and access brokering. sample_tweets.text: Since my posts have been shared here ~30 times in the past few weeks, it seems like I'm going to be contributing to Space Karen's Ketamine Extravaganza whether I like it or not.  I don't really intend to be active here, but I'll post some of the more important cybersecurity-focused stuff, since it gets screenshotted anyway. That way, people don't have to read post a week late and out of context.

This is 100% correct when looking at it from a single-system perspective. ASLR does not create a significant barrier to successful exploitation. But when looking at it from a mass-exploitation perspective, there are a lot of hidden complexities that come into play.  Vulnerability research is one of the few fields where you tend to make more money on the right side of the law. There isn't a huge demand for black market exploits. Most of the money is in bug bounty, working as a vulnerability researcher, or selling to grey-market exploit brokers.  This means that even the smallest bit of added complexity can take a vulnerability from 'cybercriminal free-for-all' to 'unlikely to be widely exploited'.   Mass-exploitation events are almost always preceded by someone publishing fully-weaponized point-and-click exploit code. It's extremely rare for criminal groups to successfully develop exploit for higher-complexity vulnerabilities on their own, even with AI.  So, less researchers capable of exploiting the bug means less chance of a working weaponized exploit being posted online. But also, the increased difficulty of exploitation, thus increased time/effort, discourages those who can exploit the bug from giving it away for free.  There's also per-target variability (which I don't know for sure is the case with this bug). But with more complex bugs, it'll sometimes be impossible to make universal exploits. In extreme cases, attackers may need to build exploit for each specific system or software version, or each specific config, or maybe even both.  So, while it's correct that it's not hard to find an ASLR bypass, it is difficult to find a bypass that works reliably at scale. So far, most of the working exploits I've seen are limited to just a handful of PHP versions, or bruteforcing ASLR. And that makes all the difference when it comes to the risk of threat actors spraying exploits at the entire internet.  For this specific exploit, the honest answer is, I don't know. It's above my pay grade. But I'm almost 100% certain that the level of bad this will be will be directly dependent on what kind of exploits security researchers make public.

Current information I have on php2Shell:  - The RCEs requires the attacker to obtain memory addresses which are typically protected by ASLR.  - I suspect the original author (lcfr_hax) likely has a reliable exploit which leads to stable code execution.  - Most of the PoCs being posted are completely non-functional AI slop.  - There is at least 1 working non-slop exploit being passed around, but it's reliant on bruteforcing for ASLR bypass, so not particularly impactful.  - Rumor of ITW exploitation are patchy. There are attempts being seen using the non-functional leaked RCE, or variants that are config / system specific.  - Some rumors point towards a known-working exploit being used by threat actors (I've personally confirmed this specific exploit works, but the ASLR bypass technique is unreliable at best and massively limits the potential impact).  - I'd expect heavy ITW exploitation in the next few weeks based on how many people are looking at this. Though, success rates will vary heavily based on the specific exploit chain.

### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 사이버 위협 환경은 AI를 활용한 자동화된 공격과 공급망 공격이 결합되어 공격 속도와 규모가 비약적으로 상승하고 있습니다. 특히 PHP 런타임의 치명적인 취약점인 'PHP2Shell'이 공개 직후 대규모로 악용되고 있으며, 공격자들은 AI 에이전트 프레임워크인 ARTEX 등을 활용해 기계적인 속도로 테넌트를 침해하고 있습니다([DarkReading](https://www.darkreading.com/cyberattacks-data-breaches/microsoft-storm-0940-connectwise-supply-chain-attack)). 또한, 소프트웨어 배포 파이프라인(PyPI 등)을 오염시켜 정보 탈취형 악성코드를 유포하는 공급망 공격이 지속적으로 보고되고 있습니다([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/litellm-release-pipeline-hacked-to-distribute-info-stealer-malware)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
*   **Storm-0940**: 중국 연계 그룹으로, AI 기반 침투 도구와 ARTEX 프레임워크를 사용하여 ConnectWise 공급망을 공격, 2,200개 이상의 테넌트를 3시간 이내에 침해함([DarkReading](https://www.darkreading.com/cyberattacks-data-breaches/microsoft-storm-0940-connectwise-supply-chain-attack)).
*   **Lazarus**: 'Operation FlashHole' 캠페인을 통해 워터링 홀 기법과 CrossWeb EX 금융 보안 소프트웨어를 악용하여 정교한 공격을 수행함([Securelist](https://securelist.com/lazarus-operation-flashhole/121541/)).
*   **TAG-217**: AI 기반 ARTEX 프레임워크를 활용하여 한국 금융 기관을 타겟으로 공격을 수행함([Recorded Future](https://www.recordedfuture.com/blog/tag-217-artex-south-korean-banks)).
*   **APT41**: Baton Drop 취약점(CVE-2022-21894)을 악용하는 BlackX UEFI 부트킷을 사용하여 중앙아시아 외교 기관을 공격함([Securelist](https://securelist.com/uefi-bootkit-blackx/121539/)).

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
*   **연세대학교**: 연세포털서비스 해킹으로 학번, 연락처, 로그인 IP 등 개인정보 유출 사고 발생([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=209012)).
*   **국립항공박물관**: 회원 1만 1,029명의 개인정보 유출 및 이를 악용한 스미싱 문자 발송 문제 제기([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=209010)).
*   **한국어 트윗([KR])**: PHP2Shell 취약점 패치 당일 공격 시도 포착, LiteLLM 자격증명 탈취, ARTEX의 분당 2,900회 테넌트 타격 등 실무적 위협 상황 공유([Twitter](https://twitter.com/ueo0j/status/2113080157552730477)).

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
*   **CVE-2026-109618 / 109619**: PHP RCE 취약점, CVSS 9.4(Critical), 전 세계적으로 대규모 악용 중([SANS ISC](https://isc.sans.edu/diary/rss/33440)).
*   **CVE-2026-110264**: GitLab RCE 취약점, 심각도 높음, 긴급 패치 권고([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5787)).
*   **CVE-2026-35029 / CVE-2026-59823**: LiteLLM 고영향 취약점, LLM 게이트웨이 침해 가능([Check Point Research](https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/when-llm-gateways-go-wrong-findings-from-litellm/)).
*   **CVE-2026-33825**: Windows Defender 로컬 권한 상승(BlueHammer), 8단계 체인 공격([Qualys Blog](https://blog.qualys.com/category/vulnerabilities-threat-research)).
*   **CVE-2022-21894**: Baton Drop 취약점, UEFI 부트킷 BlackX 악용에 사용([Securelist](https://securelist.com/uefi-bootkit-blackx/121539/)).

### 5. IOC 요약
*   **CVE**: CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619 ([SANS ISC](https://isc.sans.edu/diary/rss/33440)), CVE-2026-35029, CVE-2026-59823 ([Check Point Research](https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/when-llm-gateways-go-wrong-findings-from-litellm/)), CVE-2026-110264 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5787)), CVE-2026-33825 ([Qualys Blog](https://blog.qualys.com/category/vulnerabilities-threat-research)), CVE-2022-21894 ([Securelist](https://securelist.com/uefi-bootkit-blackx/121539/)).

### 6. 즉각 대응 권고
*   **PHP 환경 긴급 점검**: 운영 중인 모든 웹 서버의 PHP 버전을 최신으로 업데이트하고, PHP2Shell 관련 RCE 공격 징후를 EDR/XDR 로그를 통해 즉시 모니터링하십시오.
*   **공급망 자산 식별**: 조직 내 사용 중인 오픈소스 라이브러리 및 AI 게이트웨이(LiteLLM 등)의 취약
